summary: Deterministic Linux validation that an authenticated lookahead request can make real source-read progress and then have its own deadline expire in-flight without publishing any bytes, with bounded worker termination, zeroed accounting, and successful recovery. Also covers a separate already-expired-request variant and a shutdown-deadlock fix in an existing stress test.

crates/llmbridge-core/src/local_lookahea.note: content_sha256 equals the working-tree hash the stress runs executed against; file is LF, core.autocrlf=true made no change on commit

environment.cargo_target_dir: $HOME/.cache/llmbridge-wsl-target (non-native) and $HOME/.cache/llmbridge-wsl-target-native (native); isolated from Windows build artifacts

authentication.path: BoundedLocalReader::authenticate_model (Linux memfd sealed-metadata, whole-file SHA-256, real verification path)
authentication.fixture: synthetic 32-byte file 'abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz012345' created per test; authenticated by its own computed SHA-256
authentication.note: Validates the deadline/authentication/worker contract at unit level on a synthetic fixture. NOT a full GGUF-model inference run; does not touch models/stories15M-q8_0.gguf.

windows_non_native_regression.note: Windows-side; exercises the bounded_channels deadlock fix (not Linux-gated). Full Windows native lane was not run this session.

stress.note: Finite stress; does not prove absence of every possible race. Before the fix, one parallel full-suite run deadlocked for ~13 minutes (cargo 0 CPU; procfs showed the worker and test threads both parked on futex_do_wait).

same_request_in_flight_deadline.mechanism: A test-only after_read coordination hook runs in the worker AFTER the source read completes and records progress (worker_source_bytes stored) but BEFORE the post-read deadline check and any publication. Production passes None for this hook.
ordering: 1. Create synthetic fixture; authenticate via real SHA-256 (authenticate_model).
2. Schedule one range read with an initially-valid monotonic deadline (now + 500ms).
3. Worker performs the authenticated read; records source progress; reaches the after_read sync point and blocks.
4. Test confirms real same-request progress (source_bytes_read() > 0, only reachable post-successful-read).
5. Test crosses the request's own deadline with a bounded wait tied to that deadline (thread::sleep(deadline - now)); no arbitrary sleep, no timeout inflation.
6. Test releases the worker; its post-read deadline check now observes genuine expiry (Instant::now() >= deadline).
7. Consumer take() returns Interrupted; zero bytes published after expiry.
same_request_in_flight_deadline.deadline_state_transitions: valid at read start -> read completes with real progress -> deadline crossed while parked at sync point -> expired at post-read check -> terminal Interrupted, no publication
same_request_in_flight_deadline.distinction_enforced: The worker performed internal source I/O for the request, but published zero bytes to the consumer after expiry (required property: zero NEW delivery after expiration).

resource_safety.recovery: A fresh authenticated worker schedules and reads the same range successfully (bytes 'ijklmnop'); reserved_bytes back to 0.

deadlock_fix.defect: The before_read test hook blocked on barriers for every read. After release, under parallel load the worker could finish request 1 and re-enter the hook for request 2, blocking on the barrier's next generation while shutdown() waited for the worker to finish and never re-entered the barrier.
deadlock_fix.fix: Block only the first read at the barrier; later reads pass through so the worker drains and shuts down without re-entering the barrier.
deadlock_fix.scope: Test-only. Production never installs a blocking before_read hook (passes None), so production has no such deadlock.

limitations: WSL2 virtualized environment, not bare-metal; kernel is microsoft-standard-WSL2.
Deadline/authentication/worker contract validated on a synthetic 32-byte fixture via the real SHA-256 memfd path; NOT a full GGUF-model inference run.
source_bytes_read() counts include authentication whole-file hashing reads; the proof the same request completed a real read is that the after_read sync point is reached (only post-successful-read).
Finite stress (12 full-suite + 25 isolated) does not prove absence of every possible race.
Windows regression this session covered the non-native lib suite and clippy only; the full Windows native lane was not executed.
No 2 GB / dual-core physical hardware feasibility claim is made here.
